common_name: Blue Wave Hydrangea (Classic Lacecap Bigleaf Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; amend with aluminum sulfate before bud set if a truer blue is wanted, since Blue Wave's color shifts with soil pH like other bigleaf hydrangeas.

directions: Blue Wave is an old, widely grown lacecap-type bigleaf hydrangea, its flat flower heads ringed by large sterile ray florets around a flat center of small fertile florets, giving a more open, airy look than mophead types. Flower color follows soil chemistry, turning true blue in acidic soil and shifting toward pink or mauve as pH rises above neutral, so gardeners in the Gulf South's often alkaline soils may need periodic aluminum sulfate applications to hold the blue. Like other bigleaf hydrangeas, it sets flower buds on old wood the previous fall, so pruning should be limited to removing spent blooms right after flowering rather than hard cutbacks in dormancy. Give it morning sun and afternoon shade with consistently moist, well-drained soil, since the broad leaves wilt quickly in Gulf heat.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; because Wim's Red blooms on new wood, it can be cut back hard in late winter without sacrificing the coming season's flower panicles.

directions: Sold under the trade name Fire and Ice, Wim's Red is a compact, upright, early-blooming panicle hydrangea whose creamy white flowers open in late spring to early summer and then age through pink to a deep red, with reddish stems adding further color as the season progresses. Because it flowers on the current season's new wood rather than on wood from the prior year, it tolerates hard renewal pruning in late winter and is immune to bud loss from a late spring freeze, unlike bigleaf hydrangeas. It tolerates considerably more sun and a wider pH range than H. macrophylla, and its flower color is not pH-dependent. Plant in full sun to light shade with reliably moist, well-drained soil, and expect the deepest red color to develop as nights cool in early fall.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; prune hard in late winter since Brussels Lace flowers on new wood and responds with vigorous new growth and heavier bloom.

directions: Brussels Lace is an older, large-growing panicle hydrangea prized for its open, airy flower panicles, made up of a loose scattering of small fertile florets with relatively few showy sterile ray florets, giving a lacier, less dense look than heavy mophead-style paniculata cultivars like Limelight. The creamy-white conical panicles appear in mid-to-late summer on a vigorous, upright large shrub or small tree form. Since it blooms on new wood, it tolerates hard late-winter pruning and shrugs off late frosts that would ruin a bigleaf hydrangea's bud set. Give it full sun to light shade and consistently moist, well-drained soil; it tolerates more sun, cold, and a wider soil pH range than bigleaf hydrangeas, and its flower color is unaffected by soil chemistry.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; fall planting lets roots establish through the cool, mild Gulf Coast winter ahead of the heat of the following summer.

directions: Betty Sheffield Supreme is a Georgia-originated sport of the older 'Betty Sheffield' camellia, first observed in 1956, producing semi-double blooms that are pure white with a narrow band of deep pink along the petal margins; individual flowers on the same plant vary in how much color they carry. It flowers over a long midseason window on a broad, upright evergreen shrub, and its own sports have in turn produced further named camellia cultivars. Plant it in filtered, dappled shade with morning sun at most, since intense afternoon sun in the Gulf South scorches both foliage and open blooms. Keep soil consistently moist but well-drained and acidic, mulch to protect the shallow root system, and avoid disturbing the soil surface near the trunk.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade to allow root establishment before the following summer's heat.

directions: Frank Houser produces large, rose-pink peony-form to formal double flowers on a vigorous, upright, well-branched evergreen shrub, blooming in midseason and holding its form well without weather damage compared to more delicate flower shapes. Named for a Georgia camellia hybridizer, it has long been a favorite landscape and show camellia across the Deep South. Site it in filtered shade or morning sun with afternoon protection, since the Gulf Coast's intense summer sun will bleach and scorch both leaves and blooms. Provide acidic, organically rich, well-drained soil, water deeply during dry spells, and mulch well to keep the shallow roots cool and moist.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; its smaller mature size makes it well suited to foundation plantings and shaded borders.

directions: Introduced by Nuccio's Nurseries of Altadena, California, Bob's Tinsie is a compact miniature camellia grown for its brilliant red anemone-form flowers, with a dense center of narrow, curled, red-and-white streaked petaloids surrounded by a single outer ring of broader petals and bright yellow stamens. Its smaller, denser, slower-growing habit compared to full-size camellias makes it useful in tighter garden spaces or as a low hedge, and it has earned a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit. Grow it in filtered or morning shade, since strong Gulf Coast sun bleaches flower color and stresses the foliage. Plant in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil, mulch to conserve moisture over the shallow roots, and water deeply during dry spells rather than with frequent shallow watering.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall in acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; sasanquas tolerate more sun than japonicas and are commonly trained as espaliers or informal hedges.

directions: Hana Jiman is a fall-blooming sasanqua camellia with semi-double white flowers softly edged in pink, opening over a long autumn season on a dense, upright evergreen shrub with small, glossy leaves. Sasanquas like Hana Jiman tolerate considerably more direct sun than most Camellia japonica cultivars, making it a versatile choice for hedges, screens, foundation plantings, or espalier against a wall. Plant in acidic, well-drained soil enriched with organic matter, and water regularly the first year or two to establish a deep root system, after which it becomes reasonably drought tolerant. Light shearing right after flowering, if needed, keeps the naturally dense habit tidy without sacrificing next season's buds.
